subject: SIG follow-up: hosting segmentation and audit evidence for FinApps procurement
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finapps.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finapps.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: hosting detail requests

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the initial SIG packet you sent last week. Our security team reviewed sections related to hosting and asked for a clearer description of how Redwood's deployment modes map to SIG controls. Specifically:
- Which deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) has the control plane in Redwood vs customer-managed?
- For Dedicated, can you confirm whether customer data ever traverses public networks?
- For Private/VPC and on-prem, what evidence can you provide for KMS integration and audit log delivery?

We'd like this summarized in a short write-up plus any artifacts (architecture diagram, matrix mapping SIG sections to evidence). Can you provide by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Chen
Cloud Security Manager, FinApps

--
FinApps procurement: procurement@finapps.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finapps.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: hosting detail requests

Hi Olivia — thank you for the clear asks. Short version up front: Hosted = Redwood-managed control plane + data path through Redwood TLS-protected endpoints; Dedicated = control plane managed by Redwood but tenant capacity and data isolation on customer-dedicated GPUs (no public egress for customer payloads by default); Private/VPC or on-prem = customer-managed control plane or optional private control plane with customer VPC peering (control plane metadata stays in customer environment when requested).

I'm attaching two artifacts: a deployment-control-plane diagram and a hosting-segmentation matrix that maps SIG sections to the evidence we can provide (policies, config extracts, and artifacts).

Detailed answers below (high level, then mapping):

1) Control plane ownership: 
- Hosted: Redwood control plane (multi-tenant); customer data flows through our API ingress, keys are customer-managed via optional KMS integrations for token encryption-at-rest.
- Dedicated: Redwood control plane that orchestrates reserved capacity; customers can opt for a private control plane variant where control-plane APIs are logically separated and run in a dedicated management instance.
- Private/VPC or on-prem: control plane can be deployed into your VPC (private control plane) or fully on-prem. In those models control-plane telemetry and configuration are under your administrative control.

2) Network egress and data paths: 
- Hosted: requests travel over TLS to Redwood endpoints; we do not expose raw model hosts directly to the internet. We publish network boundaries and IP ranges for allowlisting.
- Dedicated: model inference happens on tenant-reserved GPUs in our environment; there is no intentional public internet egress for customer payloads. Any third-party service calls (e.g., for observability exports) are configurable and can be disabled.
- Private: no customer inference traffic leaves your environment unless explicitly configured (e.g., central logging to Redwood SaaS).

3) KMS and audit evidence: 
- Hosted: we provide evidence of customer KMS integration patterns (config snapshots, sample cloud KMS policy) and audit logs for API access.
- Dedicated: similar artifacts plus instance-level audit logs for the dedicated pool.
- Private: KMS is customer-controlled; we provide integration guides and sample proof-of-deployment artifacts (startup logs, KMS key usage metrics).

Next steps: Neha will add the SIG control mappings (A.1/A.2/etc.) and Connor will attach the specific config extracts. If you can confirm which SIG section numbers you want prioritized, we'll produce the artifact set by tomorrow EOD.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-deployment-control-plane-diagram.pdf, redwood-hosting-segmentation-matrix.xlsx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: hosting detail requests

Olivia — adding the SIG mapping you asked for. I've sketched the mapping below and included which artifact type we can produce for each control (we'll export as separate files in a follow-up):

- SIG Section: Asset Management / Cloud Infrastructure (controls related to host isolation) -> Evidence: hosting-segmentation-matrix.xlsx (row: Dedicated -> "physical tenant isolation; dedicated GPU pools; instance-level audit logs").
- SIG Section: Key Management (KMS) -> Evidence: sample KMS policy, key usage logs, integration guide (Hosted: sample config; Dedicated: config + instance logs; Private: deployment checklist).
- SIG Section: Network Security / Egress Controls -> Evidence: IP ranges file, egress policy screenshots, packet-filtering config extracts.
- SIG Section: Logging & Monitoring -> Evidence: sample API access logs (redacted), retention policy doc, screenshot of Console retention settings.

I will prepare three artifacts tonight: 1) a CSV mapping SIG controls -> artifact filenames, 2) redacted config extracts (keys replaced), 3) a short narrative that can be dropped into the SIG answer field. Connor, can you pull the dedicated-pool audit log snippet and the hosted KMS policy sample and drop them into the shared link?

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finapps.com>

Thanks Vanessa and Neha — that level of detail helps a lot. Two follow-ups from our reviewer: 
1) For Dedicated, can you provide an example network diagram showing the dedicated GPU pool and confirmation of any internal NAT (we need to ensure no transient public IPs are assigned to inference hosts).
2) For the Private VPC option, procurement wants an example DocuSign or contract clause that states control-plane telemetry retention and ownership (we need language for our legal team).

If you can send those two artifacts by EOD Friday, we'll proceed to the next stage of the SIG review.

Regards,
Olivia
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Olivia — attaching the requested examples (see shared link). Summary: 
- Dedicated network diagram attached shows dedicated GPU pool within a private subnet with egress via an internal NAT gateway that does not assign public IPs to model hosts; NAT is used for controlled updates/patching and is audited.
- Private control-plane clause: we've prepared suggested contract language that explicitly states telemetry ownership (customer) and retention windows; we can drop it into your DocuSign template or share as a redline.

Attachment stubs: dedicated-network-diagram.png (png), private-controlplane-telemetry-clause.docx (docx).

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the diagrams.
